newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary 97 inflation seen at 17.9pct - Goldman Sachs.
newsitem.headline: Hungary 97 inflation seen at 17.9pct - Goldman Sachs.

text.p: Hungary's 1997 inflation is likely to be some 17.9 percent, slightly up from the 17 percent government target, the U.S. investment bank Goldman Sachs said on Saturday, quoted by the Hungarian daily Napi Gazdasag.
1997 inflation will be as low as 17.9 percent if the government does not soften the restrictive fiscal policies of the past two years, Goldman Sachs added in a country report.
Goldman Sachs expects Hungary's inflation to begin to decline from the second quarter of the year.
The average annual inflation was about 23 percent in 1996, while year-on-year inflation stood at 20.1 percent in November.

Goldman Sachs said that the inflation rate expected for 1997 may limit the National Bank of Hungary (NBH) in cutting the monthly rate of the forint's preannounced crawling-peg devaluations as the NBH would probably want to avoid a substantial real appreciation of the Hungarian currency.
The forint is devalued by 1.2 percent monthly in the first half of this year, but the government said that the monthly rate may be reduced later if inflation would decline as expected.
Goldman Sachs also said that Hungary's gross domestic product was likely to grow by 2.1 percent in 1997, compared with the government target of between two and three percent.
